payload.rationale: Following the September 2026 decision to hike rates by 25 basis points to a 3.75-4.00% target range, the median end-2026 projection of 4.1% implies exactly one more 25 bps hike across the remaining two meetings (October and December). The Federal Reserve frequently prefers to pause between rate increases to assess incoming economic data, making a hold (0 bps hike) in October the most probable outcome before a potential final hike in December. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that elevated inflation (3.7% PCE, 3.4% core PCE) might compel the FOMC to act aggressively with consecutive hikes, raising rates in October. The strongest reason this estimate could be too low is that the Fed strongly prefers adjusting policy at December meetings when new Summary of Economic Projections are released, making an October hold almost certain.
limitations: Year-end dot projections do not identify which meeting will contain an adjustment; two scheduled meetings remain after September.
New inflation and employment information before October 28 can change policy.
Small coordinator-selected source packet; gaps remain and facts must not be confused with calibrated probabilities.
